svg.title: Fetal circulation: the three shunts that route blood around the lungs and liver
svg.desc: A schematic fetus. The placenta at the bottom sends oxygen-rich blood up the umbilical vein. Shunt one, the ductus venosus, lets most of it skip the liver and enter the inferior vena cava. In the right atrium shunt two, the foramen ovale, streams it straight into the left atrium and out the aorta to the head. What the right ventricle pumps toward the fluid-filled lungs mostly takes shunt three, the ductus arteriosus, from the pulmonary artery into the descending aorta. Two umbilical arteries carry oxygen-poor blood back to the placenta. A side panel explains each shunt, what closes it at birth and what it becomes.
svg.text: Fetal circulation: three shortcuts around the lungs
Follow the blood from the placenta. Numbers 1, 2, 3 are the shunts. Colour = how much oxygen the blood carries.
